title: Fed's Rate-Hike Odds Surge After Warsh's Inflation Warning
summary: Federal Reserve chairman Kevin Warsh used his first Jackson Hole address since replacing Jerome Powell in May to harden his inflation rhetoric, pushing the odds of a September rate hike to roughly a coin flip. The remarks matter less as a one-off signal than as a marker of a genuine break from the low-rate consensus of recent years — arriving just as the White House keeps pressing the Fed publicly to cut, testing the central bank's independence at a delicate political moment.
context:
- Warsh was confirmed as Fed chair in May 2026 in the closest Senate vote for the role in modern history, succeeding Jerome Powell amid sustained White House pressure for lower rates.

- His Jackson Hole speech recommitted the Fed to its **2%** inflation target, a sharper line than his earlier press conference, which had left investors unsure of his leanings.

- August payrolls grew **162,000**, far above forecasts, reinforcing Warsh's inflation concerns even as fellow governor Christopher Waller argued cooling price pressures could still justify holding rates steady.

title: Oil Rallies as US-Iran Conflict Escalates in the Strait of Hormuz
summary: The US and Iran have traded strikes since President Trump ordered 'major combat operations' against Tehran in February, but the conflict has now spread to the Strait of Hormuz, the corridor through which roughly **20%** of the world's seaborne crude passes. Washington's new 'tanker for tanker' policy — striking Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for attacks on commercial shipping — marks an escalation traders see as a structural threat to global fuel supply, not a fleeting shock.
context:
- The clash traces back to Trump's February order for 'major combat operations' against Iran; Tehran has since struck at least **13** commercial vessels in the strait since August.

- Washington began striking Iranian tankers directly this week under the new 'tanker for tanker' policy, a shift from years of merely policing the waterway against blockade attempts.

- US diesel prices have hit their highest level since mid-2022, as refinery damage across the Middle East and Russia leaves little spare capacity to offset the disruption.

title: Gold's Record Rally Signals a Deeper Shift Away from the Dollar
summary: Gold's climb past **$4,600** an ounce this year is not simply a reaction to this week's market swings — it reflects a structural shift in demand. Central banks bought a record 288.9 tonnes in the second quarter alone, the largest quarterly haul on record, as reserve managers diversify away from US Treasuries amid national debt above **$40 trillion** and lingering doubts about dollar-denominated assets. That sustained official buying gives this rally a firmer floor than past gold spikes.
context:
- Central banks bought a record **288.9 tonnes** of gold in the second quarter of 2026, the biggest quarterly haul on record, led by Poland and China's central banks.

- A World Gold Council survey found 45% of 76 central banks plan to keep adding to reserves over the next year, suggesting the buying trend is structural rather than opportunistic.

- Rising US government debt, now above $40 trillion, and persistent inflation concerns have eroded confidence in Treasuries, pushing reserve managers toward gold as a safer long-term store of value.
